title: Climate change
subtitle: global warming, recycle, save energy
summary: Explain the greenhouse effect and global warming, and describe what people can do to reduce it.

lesson.heading: The greenhouse effect
lesson.text: **Greenhouse gases** such as carbon dioxide, methane and ozone **exist** naturally, and they are needed to **create** the **greenhouse effect** that keeps the Earth warm enough to **support** human life.

examples.text: We don't have to make these gases; they **exist** naturally.

examples.note: create = make something happen or exist

examples.text: The Earth is warm enough to **support** human life.

lesson.heading: Global warming
lesson.text: The use of **fossil fuels** - oil, natural gas and coal - has produced **excessive** amounts of greenhouse gases. The **result** is **global warming**: an increase in the average temperature on Earth.

examples.text: **Fossil fuels** produce **excessive** amounts of carbon dioxide.
examples.note: excessive = more than you want or need

examples.text: Global warming is the **result** of more greenhouse gases.
examples.note: a result = something that happens because of something else

examples.text: Of the 15 warmest years **on record**, 14 have **occurred** since 2000.
examples.note: on record = written down or kept on a computer; occur = happen (formal)

lesson.heading: The effects of climate change
lesson.text: The **effects** of **climate change** can already be seen. Summers are getting hotter and winters wetter, so **drought** and **floods** are becoming more common. Animal and plant life is **suffering**, and some species will **disappear** altogether.

examples.text: Two **effects** of climate change are hotter summers and wetter winters.
examples.note: an effect = a change caused by something

examples.text: A **flood** is often the result of too much rain when the rivers are full.
A **drought** is a long period without rain, and droughts are occurring more often.
Illnesses such as hay fever, asthma and skin cancer are becoming more common.

lesson.heading: Destroying the environment
lesson.text: The **environment** is the air, land and water around us. If you **destroy** something, you damage it so badly that it does not exist or cannot be used. To stop global warming destroying our environment, we need to **act** now.

examples.text: The nations of the world will have to **act** together.
examples.note: act = do something to solve a problem; syn take action

lesson.heading: Six ways to reduce global warming
rows: Don't throw things away - **recycle** paper, glass and plastic.
recycle = treat something so that it can be used again
**Save energy**, e.g. switch off lights when you leave a room.
save = don't waste; energy = gas and electricity
Don't **waste** water, e.g. turn off the **tap** when you brush your teeth.
waste = use something badly; the tap is where the water comes out
Change light bulbs for more **energy-efficient** ones.
efficient = working well and not wasting energy
this reduces the fossil fuels you burn
**Plant** trees, because trees **reduce** the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
plant a tree = put a new tree in the ground; reduce = make less

lesson.heading: Verbs and nouns
lesson.note: A **solution** is the answer to a problem.

exercises.prompt: Match the words on the left with the words on the right.
Don't throw away paper, glass and plastic; ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Recycle = treat something so that it can be used again.

exercises.prompt: Don't waste water: turn off the ___ when you brush your teeth.
exercises.explanation: The tap is where the water comes out.

exercises.prompt: ___ energy by switching off lights when you leave a room.
exercises.explanation: Save energy = don't waste gas and electricity.

exercises.prompt: ___ trees in order to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide.
exercises.explanation: Plant a tree = put a new tree in the ground.

exercises.prompt: We must take ___ now, before it's too late.
exercises.explanation: Take action (syn act) = do something to solve a problem.

exercises.prompt: A long period without rain, when people do not have enough water, is a ___.
exercises.explanation: A drought is a long time without rain.

exercises.prompt: A ___ is often the result of too much rain when the rivers are full.
exercises.explanation: A flood is when water covers an area that is usually dry.

exercises.prompt: The ___ is the air, land and water around us.
If you ___ something, you damage it so badly that it cannot be used again.
If something is energy-___, it works well and doesn't waste energy.
exercises.explanation: Efficient = working well and not wasting energy.

exercises.statement: Global warming means an increase in the average temperature on Earth.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Global warming is the result of excessive greenhouse gases.

exercises.prompt: Is each word a verb or a noun?
Which word means 'the answer to a problem'?
exercises.explanation: A solution is the answer to a problem; the verb is solve.
